findings.breaking_input: An org_id that passes UUID.test but contains SQL metacharacters (e.g., '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'\; DROP TABLE org_plans --)
findings.why: The setPlan function validates the org_id as a UUID but then directly interpolates it into a SQL string without parameterization, enabling SQL injection.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries or a SQL builder instead of string interpolation.

findings.why: The setPlan function validates plan is 'free' or 'pro' but then interpolates it directly into a SQL string, allowing SQL injection through the plan value.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries; do not build SQL by concatenation even with validated inputs.

findings.breaking_input: A response with status 422 (allowed by plan for unique email violation) where the response body is a string
findings.why: The call function returns on statuses in the allow list without checking the body; a 422 with an error body could be misinterpreted as success. The allow list includes 422 for mint, but the caller doesn't validate the response.
findings.fix: After accepting an allowed non-2xx status, check that the response body meets expectations.

findings.breaking_input: A repo full name like 'owner/repo' where repo starts with uppercase
findings.why: The repoShape regex requires the repo part to start with [a-z], rejecting valid GitHub repos that start with an uppercase letter.
findings.fix: Change the regex to accept [A-Za-z] for the first character of the repo segment.

findings.breaking_input: An org_plans table that exists with the correct comment marker but no RLS enabled
findings.why: Scaffold checks RLS only after completing the migration; it does not verify that an existing table owned by launch has RLS enabled. A previous run that left RLS off (e.g., killed after migration but before RLS check) would not be detected.
findings.fix: Check RLS before running the migration as well, or ensure migration always turns RLS on.

findings.breaking_input: Two authz upstream entries, one with a valid repo and one with a valid ref, but from different contexts (e.g., different repos)
findings.why: upstreamOf takes the first match for each kind without verifying they belong to the same project. If authz reported two different repos, plans could use mismatched repo and ref.
findings.fix: Verify that the repo and ref relate to each other (e.g., by matching them against each other or requiring a single upstream entry).

findings.breaking_input: A GITHUB_TOKEN that begins with 'ghp_' (personal access token) instead of 'gho_' (OAuth token)
findings.why: The regex for GITHUB_TOKEN is /^[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}$/ which accepts any 20+ alphanumeric or underscore characters. It does not validate the token prefix (gho_, ghp_, github_pat_...), accepting tokens that have different permission models.
findings.fix: Validate the token prefix to match known GitHub token formats, or at minimum require a prefix.

findings.breaking_input: A SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN that does not start with sbp_ (e.g., sbp_ is present but with extra characters before it)
findings.why: The regex /^sbp_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}$/ allows underscores in the token body but the sbp_ prefix might appear at any position. A token with 'x_sbp_...' would be rejected but might still be valid under some configurations.
findings.fix: Ensure the validation aligns exactly with the Supabase documentation for token format.

findings.breaking_input: A shared file that is a symlink pointing outside the repository (e.g., pointing to /etc/passwd)
findings.why: The utf8 round-trip test for shared files reads the file content, but GitHub's API resolves symlinks. If the owner created a symlink that points to an unexpected location, launch's decoded content would be the symlink target, not a file it should extend.
findings.fix: Check that the 'content' field is a plain file, not a symlink or submodule, by verifying the 'type' field.

findings.breaking_input: A commit with no message (empty string) that still contains the trailer
findings.why: hasLine checks for the trailer line in the commit message. If the message is an empty string, String(msg).split('\n') returns [''] which does not contain the trailer, so the check would fail on empty messages even if the trailer exists in some other representation.
findings.fix: Handle empty or undefined message before splitting.

findings.breaking_input: A SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN with uppercase letters (e.g., SBP_XXXXXXXXX)
findings.why: The regex /^sbp_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}$/ accepts uppercase letters after the prefix, but the prefix itself is lowercase-only. Supabase tokens might start with uppercase 'SBP_' in some environments?
findings.fix: Match the exact token format documented by Supabase.

findings.breaking_input: A ref that contains characters outside the expected set (e.g., uppercase letters)
findings.why: REF regex /^[a-z0-9]{20}$/ is strictly lowercase and digits, but Supabase project refs can contain uppercase letters in some historical cases? The actual API behavior may be more permissive.
findings.fix: Test against a real Supabase ref to confirm the character set, or use case-insensitive matching.
